body: Three specific problems, in descending order of severity. (1) An internal contradiction on compute: FR-006 requires operation 'entirely on CPU-only resources, utilizing pre-computed optical flow features,' yet US-1 requires computing optical flow divergence on *newly generated* swapped videos (acceptance scenario 3, edge case on visual artifacts). Optical flow for synthetic counterfactuals cannot be pre-computed — those videos do not exist until the pipeline creates them — so either the flow must be computed on-CPU (cost unaddressed) or the ≤0.15 verification is impossible as specified. Similarly, the 'motion-only test set (objects are blurred)' requires re-extracting frozen backbone features for blurred videos, which the precomputed-feature plan does not cover. (2) The spec bakes the hypothesis into acceptance: 'it achieves at least 5% higher accuracy than the baseline' is an empirical outcome, not an acceptance criterion. A spec that fails if the (perfectly plausible) null result obtains has confused engineering validation with scientific confirmation. (3) The statistics are underpowered by design: a paired t-test over 5 seeds with a hard p<0.05 gate (SC-002, FR-005) has almost no power for realistic effect sizes; the assumptions section acknowledges this ('or the power limitation is explicitly acknowledged') but the success criteria do not. Separately, DC-001's ban on causal framing is misapplied: randomizing λ across training runs *is* the randomization the constraint demands, so the associational-only framing is stricter than the design warrants — though this errs harmlessly. The core idea (a consistency loss under counterfactual object swaps) is sound and testable; the bartender-level summary is clean. It's the plumbing around it — flow verification of videos that must be generated, blurred-test-set features, and a 5-seed significance gate — that doesn't yet hold together.

The spec is unusually honest about its own circularity — FR-004 demoting ΔAcc to a 'secondary, optimization-adjacent metric' and FR-007 supplying independent probes is exactly the right instinct, and I commend it. But there is a heretical assumption nobody has dared to question, and it sits at the foundation: that an object-swapped video retains the same action label. In Something-Something, many labels are compositional ('pretending to put something into something,' 'putting something behind something') — but many others are object-dependent in a way a cup-to-bowl swap can break or blur. The spec asserts 'Given a pair of original and counterfactual videos with the same action label' as if it were a given of the data rather than an engineering achievement that must be verified per pair. If even a modest fraction of swaps genuinely change the action, the consistency loss is not teaching motion reliance; it is teaching the model to ignore correct evidence, and the motion-only test set (objects blurred) will not distinguish these cases because blurring also removes the disambiguating cue. A per-pair label-validity check — or at minimum a human audit of whether the swap preserves the ground-truth verb — is missing from SC-005, which conflates 'manual inspection' with automated classifier-confidence and SSIM thresholds. Second, a smaller bookkeeping worry: the project description promises 'pre-computed ResNet-18 features (frozen)' while FR-001 introduces FlowNet-C for motion features; where pre-computed FlowNet-C features for Something-Something come from, and whether they fit the 14 GB disk budget, is asserted in the Assumptions but not established — the two backbone stories should be reconciled before the pipeline is built.
